name: Can I keep using my pool while part of the remodel is happening?

mainEntity.name: Can I keep using my pool while part of the remodel is happening?
mainEntity.text: Can I keep using my pool while part of the remodel is happening?

acceptedAnswer.text: In most pool remodels, the pool cannot stay fully usable during construction. Once the project involves draining, demolition, shell repairs, tile removal, coping replacement, or finish work, the pool must be closed for safety and to allow proper installation. Partial use is sometimes possible for very limited equipment-only work, but that is the exception rather than the rule. Homeowners should plan for the pool to be offline for the full construction window, plus any curing or refill time at the end. This is especially important in Los Angeles, where many people want the pool ready for warm months and special events. If the remodel is being done in stages, the contractor should explain exactly which phases require shutdown and which, if any, can happen with limited access. The best way to avoid surprises is to ask for a firm sequence before work begins. A remodel schedule should clearly state when the pool is drained, when access is restricted, and when it is safe to resume normal use.
acceptedAnswer.description: Usually no, because most pool remodel phases require draining the pool and restricting access for safety and construction. Some isolated equipment work may be possible without a full shutdown, but resurfacing, tile, coping, plumbing, and structural repairs generally require the pool to be out of service.
